<description>
This sets `permissions: contents: read` on the CI workflow, which is all the jobs use.

On this repository the token is already read-only, through the repository's default. The workflow's `permissions` key then adjusts that default ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#how-permissions-are-calculated-for-a-workflow-job)), so the setting now lives in the workflow and also holds in forks, where each owner sets the default.

The same change for libsecp256k1 is bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1964.

Closes #36512.
</description>

[How permissions are calculated for a workflow job](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#how-permissions-are-calculated-for-a-workflow-job) says the token starts from the enterprise, organization or repository default, and the workflow's `permissions` key then adjusts it. That default is not visible from outside, but each job log prints the result under *Set up job*: [this master job](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/38405322318/job/115323309543) shows `Contents: read`, `Metadata: read`, `Packages: read`. With this change `Packages` drops to none, since unlisted permissions are set to none, and no job uses it. The setting now lives in the workflow, so it also holds in forks.

Agreed on the rest: I dropped `persist-credentials: false` and the line on what the PR leaves out, and updated the description.
